claims.summary: scan_known_model_control_markers (L114) rebuilds a remainder string, re-inserting a marker only if it has a valid reference_syntax.
claims.disposition: Verified from complete source. L114-144: markers with reference_syntax.is_some() are pushed to remainder (L129-131); markers with is_none() are dropped (stripped as leaked control). Exact behavior as reported.

claims.disposition: Verified from complete source L64-86. The matches! allowlist is: appears, as, behaves, corresponds, denotes, echoes, embodies, functions, indicates, is, manifests, means, mimics, refers, replicates, represents, serves, signals. All three cited verbs present.

claims.summary: exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) and exact_reference_delimiter_pair (L153) support a wide array of Unicode quote/bracket/CJK delimiters.
claims.disposition: Verified from complete source L153-229. exact_reference_delimiter_pair enumerates ASCII + smart + CJK quote pairs (Quoted) and ASCII + fullwidth + CJK bracket pairs (Grouped); _syntax scans up to MAX depth of non-whitespace boundary chars.

claims.summary: dialogue_requested_token_band (L8) is a coarse budget classifier: 0-512, 513-1024, 1025+.
claims.disposition: Verified from complete source L8-16: >1024 -> requested_tokens_1025_plus; >512 -> 513_to_1024; else 0_to_512. Doc comment (L1-7) states it is deliberately separate from felt/spectral evidence. Exact as reported.

claims.summary: Snag hypothesis: MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH (L151) may not fully enforce the depth limit for nested markers, risking misclassification of deeply nested markers.
claims.disposition: Grounded correction (contradiction preserved, not domesticated): source DOES enforce the cap. exact_reference_delimiter_syntax collects before/after boundary chars with .take(MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH) (L208,L213), so delimiter_depth in [0,4] and saturates; deeper nesting is not misclassified, only saturated (still a recognized reference). Existing tests prove the bound (four_level, beyond_max, homogeneous_square_bracket_stack). Her nesting concern is real and already covered.

claims.summary: Snag hypothesis: first_word_after (L89) whitespace/punctuation handling (trim_matches) may be too aggressive or permissive when a newline+punctuation precedes the verb.
claims.disposition: Grounded from complete source L89-96: split_whitespace + trim of non-alphanumeric(non _) + find first non-empty means a punctuation-only or newline chunk is skipped and the next alnum word is found. Extensively covered: first_word_after_skips_leading_punctuation_transition, across_newline, multiple_punctuation_runs, non_breaking_space, internal_soft_hyphen, fails_closed_when_only_punctuation. Preserving her concern as an observed edge: preserving-a-marker is the conservative direction; no production grammar change made.

claims.summary: Suggested Next: examine L203-229 to see how MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH is applied to the delimiter_depth field.
claims.disposition: Answered by complete read of L199-229. delimiter_depth = zip of the reversed nearest-first before-scan with the after-scan, take_while consecutive pairs are declared delimiter pairs, .count(). Both scans are pre-capped at MAX (.take(4)), so delimiter_depth in [0,4]; context is set by the innermost pair (before.first/after.first). This is the exact mechanism; no change required.
